children: withdrew its full-year sales-volume and cash-flow guidance, citing worsening market conditions in China and a slower-than-expected recovery in the US.
The Swedish automaker said on Friday that lower-than-expected sales had weakened its outlook for the year, without providing replacement guidance, sending its shares down as much as 3.5% on Friday.
The company, majority-owned by China’s Geely Holding
, said the deterioration was mainly tied to a further weakening of the Chinese market and a slower recovery in the US. Europe, by contrast, remained resilient.

sold 141,609 vehicles in the third quarter, an 11% decline from a year earlier. It said industry volumes in China remained under significant pressure, with no signs of an easing in the downturn, while the recovery in the US premium-car market was slower than expected. The withdrawal marks a setback to the targets Volvo
laid out in July, when it forecast significantly stronger sales in the second half and strong positive free cash flow toward year-end.
The automaker has also faced pressure from tariffs, softer demand for electric vehicles, and high development costs. Last month, Volvo
chief Klaus Zellmer would take over as CEO within a year as the company seeks to revive sales amid intensifying competition.

title: Volvo Cars pulls sales guidance as China, US markets weaken
